summary: Creates repeated copies of the second input's channels using trigger or level timing from the first input, with optional stamping values for procedural variation.
key_concepts: Produces multiple copies of the second input along the timeline of the first input.
The first input supplies trigger signals or convolve levels, while the second input supplies the copied signal or CHOP chain.
Triggered Copy creates overlapping copies at threshold crossings; Convolve shifts and scales the second input at every first-input sample.
Output Method chooses one channel per template channel or one channel per copy channel.
Stamp Inputs recooks the second input for each triggered copy so downstream expressions can read per-copy values through fetchStamp.
Remainder controls whether partial copies are discarded, extend the output, or mix into the beginning.

key_params.name: method
key_params.note: Use first-input triggers or convolve with first-input level channels

key_params.name: output
key_params.note: How copied channels are combined in the output

key_params.name: threshold
key_params.note: Trigger threshold when Method uses trigger channels

key_params.name: keep
key_params.note: Keep copy state after the triggering event

key_params.name: copy
key_params.note: Sequence of values available as stamps

key_params.name: copy0value
key_params.note: Expression or value assigned to the stamped variable

common_gotchas: The first input controls copy timing; the second input is the signal being copied.
Stamping only affects expressions that explicitly read the stamped variables.
Trigger thresholds and remainder behavior can change copy counts without an obvious graph error.
